name: Turn a text prompt into a free AI image and a Ken Burns zoom video clip

parameters.content:
## Turn a text prompt into a free AI image + a Ken Burns zoom video clip

Types a prompt, gets back a vertical (1080x1920) MP4: a free AI image slowly zoomed in — the motion faceless-video pipelines use so a still image doesn't look static on screen. No API key, no account, no credits anywhere in this workflow.

**Pollinations** generates the image straight from a URL — no signup, no key. **FFmpeg's `zoompan` filter** animates a slow, continuous zoom over however many frames you ask for, turning a single AI image into something that reads as footage.

### How it works

1. A form takes your image prompt and how many seconds the clip should run.
2. The prompt gets a few cinematic style words appended and is URL-encoded into a Pollinations image request.
3. `curl` downloads the image to a per-run temp folder.
4. `ffmpeg` crops it to 1080x1920, applies a continuous zoom sized to your requested duration, and encodes an MP4 — no audio track, since this is the visual half only.
5. The result is checked for a clean exit code before you get the file paths back.

Drop the MP4 into an editor, or feed it into a bigger pipeline that adds voiceover and captions on top.

### Setup

- `curl` and `ffmpeg` (with `libx264`) on the PATH of the process running n8n.
- **Self-hosted n8n only.** This uses Execute Command, which n8n Cloud does not allow. n8n v2 also disables it by default — start n8n with `NODES_EXCLUDE="[]"` and `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO="/tmp"` or the file steps fail silently.

### Customization tips

Change the zoom speed or ceiling by editing `zoom+0.0012` / `1.15` in the FFmpeg command. Swap in any other keyless image API by changing the URL built in the first Code node.

## 1. Input
Your image prompt and clip length. Style words are appended automatically.

## 2. Generate the image
Pollinations builds the image straight from the URL. No key, no account.

## 3. Ken Burns zoom
FFmpeg's zoompan animates a slow continuous zoom sized to your duration.

## 4. Verify
Confirms FFmpeg exited clean before handing back the file paths.

## Self-hosted only
Execute Command does not exist on n8n Cloud. See Setup in the overview.

nodes.name: Image prompt and length form
nodes.notes: Entry point. Everything downstream reads Image Prompt and Clip Length from here.

parameters.formTitle: Text prompt to AI image + Ken Burns zoom video

values.placeholder: A lighthouse on a cliff at sunset, storm clouds gathering

parameters.formDescription: Describe an image and pick a clip length. You get back a vertical MP4 with a slow zoom-in on a free AI-generated image.

nodes.name: Build the image prompt and file paths
nodes.notes: One /tmp folder per submission so runs never overwrite each other. Appends cinematic style words to the raw prompt.

nodes.name: Create the temp folder
nodes.notes: mkdir -p is safe to run again.

nodes.name: Download the AI image (Pollinations)
nodes.notes: Free, no account, no key. Retries a few times since Pollinations can be slow under load. Reads paths from the Code node, not $json: an Execute Command node replaces the item with its own stdout/stderr/exitCode.

parameters.command: =curl -fsS --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors --max-time 120 -o "{{ $('Build the image prompt and file paths').item.json.imagePath }}" "{{ $('Build the image prompt and file paths').item.json.imageUrl }}"

nodes.name: Render the Ken Burns zoom video (FFmpeg)
nodes.notes: zoompan's d (frame count) is sized to your requested Clip Length so the zoom always finishes exactly at the end of the clip. Reads paths from the Code node, not $json, for the same reason as the download step.

parameters.command: =ffmpeg -y -loop 1 -i "{{ $('Build the image prompt and file paths').item.json.imagePath }}" -t {{ $('Build the image prompt and file paths').item.json.seconds }} -vf "scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1080:1920,zoompan=z='min(zoom+0.0012,1.15)':d={{ $('Build the image prompt and file paths').item.json.zoomFrames }}:s=1080x1920:fps={{ $('Build the image prompt and file paths').item.json.fps }}" -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p "{{ $('Build the image prompt and file paths').item.json.videoPath }}"

nodes.name: Verify the render succeeded
nodes.notes: Throws with the real FFmpeg stderr if the exit code was not 0, instead of silently returning a broken file path.
